synopsis: For the off-road scope discussed, US rules require warnings, detection and written safety programs that evaluate technologies, but not automatic braking; the MSHA surface-mobile-equipment rule was finalised on 20 December 2023, became effective on 19 January 2024, and had a compliance date of 17 July 2024, with 863 citations reported by April 2026 [f2861, f2087, f2777, f2088]. Powered haulage caused 13 of 33 US mining deaths (39%) and 426 of 4,792 nonfatal injuries (9%) in 2025, supporting its continued importance as a safety priority [f2978, f2979, f2980]. Historical evidence distinguishes collision hazards from other haul-truck hazards: among 54 deaths in January 2005–June 2021, 13 were collisions with people or vehicles, 21 involved berms and 12 occurred at dump points; 12 of the 13 collisions involved forward movement, while a separate blind-area dataset found 67% of victims behind reversing equipment [f2989, f2990, f2986]. MSHA Table M-1 uses approximately 2.94 m/s² constant deceleration, weight-dependent system response of 0.5–2.5 seconds and one second of operator response, whereas a historic mining report gives approximately two seconds of nominal operator reaction and another 1–2 seconds of dynamic-retarder lag [f5989, f6058, f6059, f6060]. US on-road evidence offers threshold-and-latency evaluation methods and cautions about false or unexpected braking, but FMVSS No. 127 is not applicable to off-road machines and the final status of the July 2023 heavy-vehicle AEB proposal remains uncertain [f6346, f6189, f6304, f2831, f1964]. Regulatory compliance should not be treated as proof of proximity-detection feasibility, and the corpus found no dedicated US off-road requirement for an ML collision-avoidance function to meet a specified ML validation standard by 2028 [f11228, f2393].
